p.i: buscunque ratiunculis; quoniam in hac disciplina fundamenta haberentur perpetuae vt veritatis, ita certissimae solidissimae atque evidentissimae demonstrationis. Quibus fundamentis firmiter positis ad Philosophiam postmodum discendam paratiores euaderent, alioquin inutiles futuri auditores rerum earum, quarum pleraeque non tam firmae essent fidei, quam certae dubitationis: adeo vt Plato Xenocrates & alii eorum sectatores neminem ad Philosophicas lectiones admitterent, nisi quem in Mathematicis bene nouerant instructum; opinati nimirum, non solum frustra aliquem sine legitimis adminiculis & velut illotis manibus ac pedibus ad secretiora Philosophiae adyta accedere, sed etiam praeposterè discì docerique illa, quae magis humani ingenii acumine tanquam vago non nunquam & incerto niterentur, quam indubitatis, solidis, immotis, aeternisque funda-

page.notes: The text is in a italic roman hand with long s rendered as s; the first line is a continuation from the previous page. The catchword "funda-" stands at the foot right. The printed word "buscunque" is probably "quibuscunque" with the opening letters cut off by the binding edge; marked as read. Words such as "ratiunculis" and "Quibus" are read from the scan; no [?] needed for clear forms.
